entries.title: Neuro-ICU targets (rounds lookup)
entries.scopeNote: Rounds lookup, not a protocol. Glucose and temperature are intentionally not on this card. aSAH-specific numbers: see aSAH numbers card.

rows.target: Avoid hyponatremia
notes: Hyponatremia can worsen cerebral edema
Correction limits for chronic hyponatremia: see hyponatremia-ods
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7

rows.condition: During hypertonic saline for ICP or edema
rows.target: Upper limit Na 155–160 mEq/L; Cl 110–115 mEq/L
notes: A ceiling to limit AKI, not a treatment goal
Avoid severe hypernatremia and hyperchloremia (AKI association)
Monitor Na, Cl and renal function routinely; frequency from BID to q2h depending on how fast values are moving
evidenceNote: Cook 2020: ceiling — conditional, very low-quality evidence
Cook 2020: avoid severe hyperNa/hyperCl — conditional, low-quality evidence
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7

rows.condition: Hypertonic saline for ICP or edema — SAH
rows.target: Symptom-based bolus HTS rather than dosing to a sodium target
notes: Studies that targeted sodium used 145–155 mEq/L; data too limited to recommend a target
No HTS dosing strategy is recommended to improve neurological outcome
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7

rows.condition: Hypertonic saline for ICP or edema — ICH
rows.target: Either bolus dosing or a targeted sodium is acceptable
notes: Targeted studies used 145–155 mEq/L; results conflicting
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7

rows.condition: Hypertonic saline for ICP or edema — TBI, AIS; continuous infusion to a sodium goal (any condition)
rows.target: No sodium target recommended
notes: TBI: no substantial evidence for targeting a specific sodium
AIS: continuous 3% to 145–155 mEq/L didn't consistently reduce ICP crises or improve outcome (2 conflicting studies)
Any condition: insufficient evidence that a continuous infusion to a sodium goal improves outcome
evidenceNote: Cook 2020: evidence summary / insufficient-evidence statement — no recommendation made
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7

rows.target: Follow the osmolar gap, not a serum osmolality threshold
notes: No gap cutoff is recommended: 20 mOsm/kg is used in practice but unsupported; one study correlated a gap ≥55 mOsm/kg with mannitol concentration
Recent studies: osmolality >320 mOsm/L did not change AKI incidence
Monitor renal function closely (good practice)
evidenceNote: Cook 2020: no gap cutoff — insufficient evidence
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7

rows.target: 60–70 mm Hg
notes: Whether 60 or 70 is the minimum is unclear; may depend on autoregulatory status
No CPP target from a provided source for aSAH, ICH or AIS
evidenceNote: BTF 4th ed: Level II B (low-quality evidence)
sources: Brain Trauma Foundation. Guidelines for the Management of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury, 4th Edition. 2016; ch. 17 Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Thresholds

rows.target: Avoid aggressive fluids and pressors to hold CPP >70 mm Hg
notes: Risk of adult respiratory failure
sources: Brain Trauma Foundation. Guidelines for the Management of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury, 4th Edition. 2016; ch. 17 Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Thresholds

sections.heading: Hemoglobin — trial findings, not guideline targets

rows.condition: Acute brain injury with Hb <9 g/dL (TBI 59%, aSAH 23%, ICH 18%) — TRAIN
rows.target: Transfusing at <9 vs <7 g/dL: less unfavorable outcome at 180 days
notes: Unfavorable outcome (GOS-E 1–5): 62.6% vs 72.6%; adjusted RR 0.86 (95% CI 0.79–0.94)
≥1 cerebral ischemic event: 8.8% vs 13.5% (RR 0.65, 0.44–0.97)
Median 2 vs 0 units; strategy applied up to 28 days
Clinical teams unblinded; outcome assessors blinded
sources: Taccone FS, et al. Restrictive vs Liberal Transfusion Strategy in Patients With Acute Brain Injury: The TRAIN Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2024;332:1623-1633. doi:10.1001/jama.2024.20424

rows.target: Transfusing at ≤10 (mandatory) vs ≤8 g/dL (optional): no significant difference in 12-month outcome
notes: 12-month mortality 27.2% vs 27.1%; DCI and new infarction similar
Radiographic vasospasm (secondary): 31.5% vs 40.7% (RR 0.77, 0.63–0.95)
Thresholds held through day 21; median 2 vs 0 units
sources: English SW, et al. Liberal or Restrictive Transfusion Strategy in Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (SAHARA). N Engl J Med 2025;392:1079-1088. doi:10.1056/NEJMoa2410962

pitfalls: Don't treat 145–155 mEq/L as a guideline target — it's the range used in studies (Cook 2020)
TRAIN and SAHARA used different thresholds and outcomes; TRAIN's aSAH subgroup was 23% of patients
keyNumbers: No sodium goal endorsed for ICP; avoid hyponatremia
Mannitol: follow osmolar gap, not osm 320
sources: Cook AM, et al. Guidelines for the Acute Treatment of Cerebral Edema in Neurocritical Care Patients (NCS). Neurocrit Care 2020;32:647-666. doi:10.1007/s12028-020-00959-7
Brain Trauma Foundation. Guidelines for the Management of Severe Traumatic Brain Injury, 4th Edition. 2016; ch. 17 Cerebral Perfusion Pressure Thresholds
Taccone FS, et al. Restrictive vs Liberal Transfusion Strategy in Patients With Acute Brain Injury: The TRAIN Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA 2024;332:1623-1633. doi:10.1001/jama.2024.20424

entries.title: aSAH numbers
entries.scopeNote: Rounds lookup, not a protocol. Glucose and temperature (Hoh §8 Recs 7–8) intentionally omitted. Hb thresholds: see Neuro-ICU targets card.

rows.target: No specific SBP target — frequent BP monitoring, short-acting agents; avoid severe hypotension, hypertension and BP variability
notes: Severe hypertension (>180–200 mm Hg): lower gradually; avoid MAP <65 (writing-group text)
Earlier guidelines used SBP <160 or <180 — may be reasonable, evidence insufficient for a target
Meta-analysis: more rebleeding with SBP >160, not with <140
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Emergency reversal
notes: Follow current standards for life-threatening bleeding
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Not useful to improve functional outcome
notes: ULTRA: ultra-early TXA didn't improve 6-month outcome
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §6 Rec 3: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE A
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: 60 mg enteral q4h × 21 days; start as soon as possible, within 96 h of onset
notes: Keep giving through hypotension that standard measures can manage; hold temporarily only for significant BP variability (Hoh text)
Cirrhosis: 30 mg q4h with close BP/HR monitoring (label)
1 h before or 2 h after meals; avoid grapefruit (label)
Can't swallow: puncture both capsule ends with an 18 G needle, draw contents into an oral/enteral syringe labeled 'Not for IV Use', give via NG/PEG, flush with 30 mL NS (label)
Never IV or other parenteral route — boxed warning (label)
Strong CYP3A4 inhibitors contraindicated; strong inducers (phenytoin, carbamazepine, phenobarbital, rifampin) generally not co-administered (label)
IV and intra-arterial nimodipine: too little data to recommend (Hoh)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436
Nimodipine capsules US prescribing information. Bionpharma Inc.; revised 12/2025 (DailyMed label)

rows.target: Frequent GCS or NIHSS to monitor DCI and other complications
notes: Peak DCI/vasospasm risk: post-bleed days 6–10 (Hoh §8.3 text)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Can be useful to detect vasospasm and predict DCI
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Reasonable to detect vasospasm and predict DCI
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Can be useful to predict DCI
notes: Order/consult item; interpretation by neurophysiology
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Brain tissue O2, lactate/pyruvate, glutamate may be considered to predict DCI
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Euvolemia — close monitoring and goal-directed treatment
notes: CVP alone isn't an adequate measure of volume status
Definitions of euvolemia vary; no clear standard
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Potentially harmful — excess morbidity
notes: RCTs: more complications without less DCI or better outcome
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8 Rec 5: COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: No prophylactic hemodynamic augmentation
notes: No outcome benefit; more complications including heart failure (Hoh text)
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.3 Rec 8: COR 3: Harm, LOE B-R
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Mineralocorticoid (fludrocortisone) is reasonable
notes: RCTs: less natriuresis, urine volume, hyponatremia and IV fluid use; DCI and outcome not consistently improved
Main adverse effect: hypokalemia — potassium supplementation
High-dose hydrocortisone: similar sodium effects, more complications (hyperglycemia, hypokalemia, GI bleeding, heart failure)
No dose in the provided sources — use pharmacy dosing
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Raising SBP may be reasonable to limit DCI
notes: Hoh Figure 3 labels its DCI-response box (elevate BP, ensure euvolemia, imaging) Class 2a; the recommendation table says 2b — table used
Retrospective: more neurological improvement with norepinephrine than phenylephrine (94% vs 71%)
HIMALAIA (only RCT) stopped early, underpowered
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: IA vasodilator therapy and/or cerebral angioplasty may be reasonable
notes: Neuro-IR decision
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.3 Rec 4 (IA vasodilators): COR 2b, LOE B-NR
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Not recommended
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.3 Rec 6: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE A
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Not recommended
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.3 Rec 7: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE A
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.condition: Fluctuating exam, depressed mental state, ruptured MCA aneurysm, high-grade SAH, ICH, hydrocephalus or cortical infarction
rows.target: Reasonable to detect seizures
notes: Order/consult item; interpretation by neurophysiology
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.condition: High seizure-risk features (ruptured MCA aneurysm, high-grade SAH, ICH, hydrocephalus, cortical infarction)
rows.target: Prophylactic ASM may be reasonable
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Not beneficial
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.5 Rec 3: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE B-R
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Avoid — excess morbidity and mortality
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.5 Rec 4: COR 3: Harm, LOE B-NR
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Treat ≤7 days (perioperative period)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.condition: Presented with seizures, no prior epilepsy
rows.target: >7 days doesn't reduce future SAH-associated seizure risk
evidenceNote: Hoh 2023 §8.5 Rec 6: COR 3: No Benefit, LOE B-NR
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

rows.target: Pharmacological or mechanical prophylaxis
notes: Small RCT: enoxaparin 40 mg SC daily after aneurysm treatment didn't increase bleeding
Optimal timing relative to securing and procedures is unclear (Hoh text)
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436

pitfalls: Don't stop nimodipine for manageable hypotension — interruptions were associated with more DCI (Hoh text)
Nimodipine plus phenytoin: phenytoin is both a strong CYP3A4 inducer (label) and harmful as SAH prophylaxis (Hoh)
keyNumbers: Nimodipine 60 mg q4h × 21 d (30 mg q4h in cirrhosis)
Unsecured: no SBP target; avoid MAP <65 and BP swings
Euvolemia; no prophylactic hypervolemia or augmentation
Seizure ppx only if high-risk; no phenytoin; ASM ≤7 d
sources: Hoh BL, et al. 2023 Guideline for the Management of Patients With Aneurysmal Subarachnoid Hemorrhage (AHA/ASA). Stroke 2023;54:e314-e370. doi:10.1161/STR.0000000000000436
Nimodipine capsules US prescribing information. Bionpharma Inc.; revised 12/2025 (DailyMed label)

entries.title: Thrombophilia tests: validity by timing and anticoagulant
entries.scopeNote: Whether each result can be trusted during acute thrombosis or on UFH/LMWH, a VKA or a DOAC. Inherited thrombophilia testing rarely changes default antiplatelet therapy after arterial stroke unless it shows APS or venous thrombosis (Kleindorfer 2021). AT, protein C and protein S deficiency can be acquired, and levels vary within a person (Middeldorp 2023). "Not addressed by sources" means no source in this app covers that cell.

notes.text: IgM rheumatoid factor can falsely raise IgM aCL/aβ2GPI; avoid hemolyzed, icteric or lipemic samples. Interpret together with the LA result.

cells.text: Many reagents neutralize heparin; false positives at supratherapeutic anti-Xa. LMWH: draw ≥12 h after the dose, near the next one, with an anti-Xa level

cells.text: False positives and negatives; mixing with normal plasma is not reliable. If feasible, test 1–2 weeks after stopping the VKA (LMWH bridge if needed)

cells.text: False positives even at low DOAC levels. If feasible, hold the DOAC ≥48 h (longer with renal impairment) and check a DOAC level; adsorbents only with lab input

entries.scopeNote: Rounds lookup for hospitalized adults with PD on dopaminergic therapy — not a protocol. Get movement-disorder input early when the usual regimen can't be given.

rows.target: Keep the usual drugs, doses and dose times; resume the usual dose as soon as oral medication is allowed
notes: Labels: carbidopa-levodopa can continue up to anesthesia while oral medication is permitted; if interrupted, watch for an NMS-like syndrome
Abrupt reduction or withdrawal can cause hyperpyrexia, rigidity and altered consciousness — see acute-neuro:nms-parkinsonism-hyperpyrexia
Engage neurology / movement disorders early if the usual regimen can't be given (BMJ; Hwang)

rows.condition: Use BMJ's own factors, not calc:ledd
rows.target: A = levodopa mg/day (×0.7 if CR), then ×1.3 if on a COMT inhibitor. B = agonist mg/day × factor (ropinirole 20, rotigotine 20, pramipexole base 100, cabergoline 100, bromocriptine 10, apomorphine 10). LEDD = A + B
notes: Levodopa dose excludes carbidopa
calc:ledd uses Jost 2023 factors, which differ (CR 0.75; COMT +0.33 or +0.5 of covered levodopa; pramipexole base 142.86; rotigotine 30.3) — don't feed its result into these steps

rows.target: Adjusted LEDD = LEDD × 0.55; rotigotine mg/24 h = adjusted LEDD ÷ 20, rounded to the nearest 2 mg, once daily
notes: BMJ rounds up to 16 mg; the US label maximum is 6 mg/24 h (early PD) and 8 mg/24 h (advanced PD) — doses above 8 mg exceed the label
Example: levodopa IR 300 mg/day → 300 × 0.55 = 165 → 8.25 → 8 mg/24 h
Example: levodopa IR 600 mg/day → 330 → 16.5 → 16 mg/24 h per BMJ (twice the label maximum)
BMJ: the ×0.55 deliberately starts below equivalence; review and adjust early; may be too weak for high-dose regimens

Capsule may be opened onto soft food; tube use not addressed in the label

pitfalls: calc:ledd (Jost 2023) and the BMJ algorithm use different factors — don't mix them
BMJ's adjusted LEDD >350 mg branch (continuous SC apomorphine with domperidone pre-load) is not on this card: the Apokyn label covers intermittent pen doses only (≤6 mg per dose)
